suggested_record.title: Responsive presentation CSS must not resurrect semantically suppressed surfaces
suggested_record.summary: A mobile hardsub regression persisted because responsive rules using display:flex/block !important had higher selector specificity than a semantic .hardsub-strategy-suppressed rule. The UI state correctly marked the inactive execution surface as suppressed, but presentation CSS made it visible again. The fix adds stage-aware selectors and a higher-specificity semantic gate keyed by data-media-operation and data-hardsub-strategy. Candidate lesson: semantic visibility state must outrank presentation/layout restoration rules, and regression tests should assert the rendered surface rather than only class presence.
